item.title: EDITORIAL: Stay steadfast on fossil fuels lawsuit
item.description: One day before Gov. Josh Green’s administration filed its lawsuit last May against fossil fuel companies for lying to and misleading the public about carbon pollution and climate change, the federal administration made an unusual pre-emptive strike — suing Hawaii by stating that the U.S. Clean Air Act reserves claims against energy companies to federal offices.

item.title: TAX MAN: Idle land and natural resource funds
item.description: Earlier this year, we started looking at reports of agencies that have administratively established special funds. We noted some fairly large nest eggs controlled by the Department of Education and the Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity. This week we will turn our attention to the Department of Land and Natural Resources because we wouldn’t want them to feel left out! Their report to the Legislature is here.

item.title: Agreement aims for Navy mission success, bird conservation
item.description: KILAUEA — Work is underway on the $800,000 collaborative agreementbetween the U.S. Navy and the Friends of Kauai Wildlife Refuge that supports a multi-year project focused on expanding habitat for native seabirds and water birds, support aviation safety at the Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF) by reducing Bird Aircraft Strike Hazard (BASH) and advancing long-term conservation on Kauai.

item.title: Mayoral candidates make it official
item.description: LIHUE — Mel Rapozo and Bernard Carvalho Jr. made good on earlier public announcements of their intentions to run for the mayor.

item.title: Free tax preparations start Tuesday
item.description: LIHUE — The AARP Foundation Tax-Aide volunteer corps announces that the free 2025 tax return preparation service starts on Tuesday at the Lihue Neighborhood Center from 9 a.m. on a no-reservation, first come, first served basis.

item.title: Hawaii had one of hottest, driest years on record in 2025, UH report finds
item.description: Last year was one of the driest and warmest on rec­ord in the state, with the temperature being above average each month and rainfall below average in all but one month, according to the Hawai‘i Annual Climate Report from University of Hawaii.

item.title: Public invited to nominate kupuna for Older Americans Month
item.description: LIHUE — The Agency on Elderly Affairs invites the community to participate in honoring older adults who have made meaningful and lasting contributions to the island of Kauai.

item.title: Global rivals start to gain ground amid flat growth
item.description: Hawaii entered 2026 with a visitor industry still well below its prepandemic peak, and new forecasts point to another year of modest gains as Maui’s recovery drags and international markets — especially Japan and Canada — continue to lag.

item.title: Top science projects advancing to states
item.description: LIHUE — The wind howled through trees and the rain pelted the Kauai War Memorial Convention Hall parking lot where attendees to the Kauai Regional Science and Engineering Fair on Saturday jockeyed their cars for parking closest to the convention hall, minimizing exposure to the wind and rain.
